newsitem.title: INDIA: India plans to eliminate leprosy by 2000.
newsitem.headline: India plans to eliminate leprosy by 2000.

text.p: India has vowed to eliminate leprosy as a public health problem by the turn of the century, World Health Organisation (WHO) officials said on Thursday.

Health ministers from at least 15 of 20 countries accounting for 93 percent of the world's leprosy patients, are expected to participate in a three-day conference on the eradication of the disease beginning in Delhi on Friday, they said.
Around 680,000 people, or 52 percent of the world's 1.26 million leprosy patients, are in India.
Indian officials say they want to propagate new methods of prevention and cure of the disease by taking their campaign to remote areas.

"Particular emphasis will be placed to take MDT (multi-drug therapy) to hitherto hidden and untreated cases, and to areas and populace beyond the reach of general health services," said S.K. Noordeen, director of a leprosy combat programme.
Leprosy is a skin disease that affects the mucous membrane and the nerves. If untreated, it can cause permanent damage to limbs and eyes.
